question: Which of the following is INCORRECT in relation to the Indian political system? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (02/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Parliamentary system of government
Secular state
Presidential system of government
Quasi federal system
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Presidential system of government

Explanation:
India follows a parliamentary system of government where the President is the constitutional head and the Prime Minister is the real executive head. A presidential system, like that of the USA, has the President as both the head of state and government, separate from the legislature. India is a secular state, meaning no official religion and equal treatment for all religions. India is described as a quasi-federal system because it combines federal and unitary features, such as a single constitution, single citizenship, and central dominance. Thus, the presidential system is not part of the Indian political system.

☛ India's government system → Parliamentary
☛ Real executive head in India → Prime Minister
☛ Constitutional head in India → President
☛ Example of presidential system → USA
☛ India's federal nature → Quasi-federal
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा भारतीय राजनीतिक व्यवस्था के संबंध में गलत है? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (02/12/2024) Shift 3)

धर्मनिरपेक्ष राज्य
राष्ट्रपति शासन प्रणाली
अर्द्ध संघीय प्रणाली
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है राष्ट्रपति शासन प्रणाली

Explanation:
भारत में संसदीय शासन प्रणाली है, जिसमें राष्ट्रपति संवैधानिक प्रमुख होता है और प्रधानमंत्री कार्यपालिका का वास्तविक प्रमुख होता है। राष्ट्रपति शासन प्रणाली अमेरिका जैसे देशों में पाई जाती है, जहां राष्ट्रपति कार्यपालिका का प्रमुख होता है और विधायिका से अलग होता है। भारत एक धर्मनिरपेक्ष राज्य है, जहां राज्य का कोई आधिकारिक धर्म नहीं है और सभी धर्मों को समान संरक्षण प्राप्त है। भारत को अर्द्ध संघीय प्रणाली कहा जाता है क्योंकि यह संघीय और एकात्मक विशेषताओं का मिश्रण है, जैसे कि एक संविधान, एक नागरिकता और केंद्र की प्रधानता। इसलिए, राष्ट्रपति शासन प्रणाली भारतीय राजनीतिक व्यवस्था से संबंधित नहीं है।

question: Which of the following authorities constitute the Ethics Committee in the Rajya Sabha? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (02/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The President
The Prime Minister
The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha

Explanation:
The Ethics Committee in the Rajya Sabha is constituted by the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. This committee examines matters related to the conduct and ethics of members. It was first formed in 1997. The committee consists of 10 members, who are nominated by the Chairman. It plays a crucial role in ensuring transparency and accountability in parliamentary democracy. The tenure of the committee is one year.

question: Which of the following committees suggested that the 'duty to pay taxes' should also be a Fundamental Duty of the Indian citizen? (RRB JE CBT-I 2024 (16/12/2024) Shift 1)
options: Sarkaria Commission
Justice JS Verma Committee
Swaran Singh Committee
Santhanam Committee
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Swaran Singh Committee

Explanation:
The Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976). The Swaran Singh Committee made recommendations regarding Fundamental Duties. It suggested that 'duty to pay taxes' should also be a Fundamental Duty, but it was not finally included. Currently, there are 11 Fundamental Duties under Article 51A. The Swaran Singh Committee's recommendations led to the inclusion of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution.

☛ Which committee suggested duty to pay taxes? → Swaran Singh Committee

question: Which of the following articles deal with the provisions regarding the election, qualification, and removal of the Vice-President of India?  (RRB JE CBT-I 2024 (16/12/2024) Shift 1)
options: Article 224 - 245
Article 68 - 75
Article 78 - 80
Article 63 - 71
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 63 - 71

Explanation:
The Constitution of India deals with the Vice-President in Articles 63 to 71. Article 63 establishes the office of the Vice-President. Article 64 makes the Vice-President the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. Article 66 describes the election process, which is done by the members of Parliament through single transferable vote. Article 67 provides for the term (5 years) and removal process, requiring a resolution passed by the Rajya Sabha. Article 68 deals with election to fill a vacancy. Article 69 covers the oath, and Article 71 deals with disputes related to the election. Other options like Articles 224-245 pertain to the judiciary.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ What is the term of the Vice-President? → 5 years
☛ Which article covers the removal of the Vice-President? → Article 67
☛ Which article describes the election of the Vice-President? → Article 66
☛ Which article makes the Vice-President the Chairman of Rajya Sabha? → Article 64
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-से अनुच्छेद भारत के उपराष्ट्रपति के चुनाव, योग्यता और निष्कासन के प्रावधानों से संबंधित हैं? (RRB JE CBT-I 2024 (16/12/2024) Shift 1)
options_hi: अनुच्छेद 224 - 245
अनुच्छेद 68 - 75
अनुच्छेद 78 - 80
अनुच्छेद 63 - 71
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 63 - 71

Explanation:
भारत का संविधान उपराष्ट्रपति से संबंधित प्रावधान अनुच्छेद 63 से 71 में करता है। अनुच्छेद 63 में उपराष्ट्रपति पद का प्रावधान है। अनुच्छेद 64 के अनुसार उपराष्ट्रपति राज्यसभा का पदेन सभापति होता है। अनुच्छेद 66 में चुनाव प्रक्रिया वर्णित है, जहां सांसदों का एकल संक्रमणीय मत द्वारा चुनाव होता है। अनुच्छेद 67 में कार्यकाल (5 वर्ष) और पद से हटाने की प्रक्रिया है, जिसमें राज्यसभा में प्रस्ताव पारित करना आवश्यक है। अनुच्छेद 68 में रिक्ति की स्थिति में चुनाव का प्रावधान है। अनुच्छेद 69 में शपथ और अनुच्छेद 71 में निर्वाचन विवादों का समाधान शामिल है। अन्य विकल्प जैसे 224-245 न्यायपालिका से संबंधित हैं।

question: Every year, Foreign Trade Policy has been declared by which ministry of the Government of India?  (RRB JE CBT-I 2024 (16/12/2024) Shift 1)
options: Ministry of Information
Ministry of Home Affairs
Ministry of External Affairs
Ministry of Commerce and Industry
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ministry of Commerce and Industry

Explanation:
The Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) of India is annually declared by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. This policy aims to boost India's exports and imports and is implemented by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT). The FTP focuses on economic growth, employment generation, and enhancing India's global competitiveness. It includes various export promotion schemes, duty exemptions, and trade facilitation measures. The current Minister of Commerce and Industry is Piyush Goyal. The policy is typically announced for a period of five years but is reviewed annually to adapt to changing global trade dynamics.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which ministry announces Foreign Trade Policy? → Ministry of Commerce and Industry
☛ Which department implements FTP? → Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT)
☛ Who is the current Minister of Commerce and Industry? → Piyush Goyal
☛ What is the main objective of FTP? → Promoting exports and imports
☛ For how many years is FTP usually issued? → Five years (with annual review)
question_hi: भारत सरकार के किस मंत्रालय द्वारा प्रतिवर्ष विदेश व्यापार नीति घोषित की जाती है? (RRB JE CBT-I 2024 (16/12/2024) Shift 1)
options_hi: सूचना मंत्रालय
गृह मंत्रालय
विदेश मंत्रालय
वाणिज्य और उद्योग मंत्रालय
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है वाणिज्य और उद्योग मंत्रालय

Explanation:
भारत सरकार की विदेश व्यापार नीति (FTP) प्रतिवर्ष वाणिज्य और उद्योग मंत्रालय द्वारा घोषित की जाती है। यह नीति भारत के निर्यात और आयात को बढ़ावा देने के लिए बनाई जाती है और इसे विदेश व्यापार महानिदेशालय (DGFT) द्वारा कार्यान्वित किया जाता है। FTP का मुख्य उद्देश्य आर्थिक विकास, रोजगार सृजन और वैश्विक बाजार में भारत की प्रतिस्पर्धात्मकता को बढ़ाना है। यह नीति विभिन्न निर्यात प्रोत्साहन योजनाओं, शुल्क छूट और व्यापार सुविधा उपायों को शामिल करती है। वर्तमान में, वाणिज्य एवं उद्योग मंत्री पीयूष गोयल हैं।

question: Which of the following articles deals with the office of the special officer for Linguistic Minorities? (RRB JE CBT-I 2024 (16/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: 350-B
351-B
351-A
350-A
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 350-B

Explanation:
Article 350-B of the Indian Constitution deals with the office of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities. This officer is appointed by the President and is tasked with investigating all matters relating to the safeguards provided for linguistic minorities under the Constitution and reporting to the President. This provision was added after the States Reorganisation Act of 1956 to protect the rights of linguistic minorities. Article 350-A directs state governments to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother tongue to children of linguistic minorities. The Special Officer ensures that these safeguards are implemented effectively, thereby promoting linguistic diversity and protecting minority rights.

question: What is the key difference between the Supreme Court’s original jurisdiction in federal disputes versus its writ jurisdiction? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Federal dispute jurisdiction is exclusive to SC, while writ jurisdiction is concurrent with High Courts.
Federal dispute jurisdiction can be exercised suo moto, while writ jurisdiction requires a petition.
Federal dispute jurisdiction applies to civil matters, while writ jurisdiction applies to criminal matters.
Federal dispute jurisdiction is advisory, while writ jurisdiction is binding.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Federal dispute jurisdiction is exclusive to SC, while writ jurisdiction is concurrent with High Courts.

Explanation:
Under Article 131 of the Indian Constitution, the Supreme Court has exclusive original jurisdiction over federal disputes between the Centre and States or between States. This means such disputes can only be filed in the Supreme Court, not in any High Court. On the other hand, writ jurisdiction is available both in the Supreme Court (under Article 32) and in High Courts (under Article 226), making it concurrent. Citizens can approach either court for enforcement of fundamental rights through writs. This is the key distinction: federal jurisdiction is exclusive to the Supreme Court, while writ jurisdiction is shared with High Courts.

☛ What type of jurisdiction does the Supreme Court have in federal disputes? → Exclusive and original

question: What happens if an Indian citizen voluntarily becomes a citizen of another country? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Their Indian citizenship ends automatically
They must get government approval
They become dual citizens.
Nothing changes.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Their Indian citizenship ends automatically

Explanation:
As per the Indian Constitution and the Citizenship Act, 1955, India does not allow dual citizenship. If an Indian citizen voluntarily acquires citizenship of another country, their Indian citizenship automatically terminates. This provision is covered under Section 9 of the Citizenship Act. It means the person loses the Indian passport and other citizenship rights. No government approval or formality is required; the process is automatic. The Indian Constitution provides for single citizenship, which strengthens national unity. This rule applies regardless of the country whose citizenship is acquired. The person cannot retain Indian citizenship while holding another country's citizenship.

☛ Type of citizenship in India → Single citizenship (no dual citizenship).
☛ Part 2 of Indian Constitution → Provisions related to citizenship (Articles 5-11).
☛ On acquiring foreign citizenship → Indian passport becomes invalid automatically.
☛ OCI card in India → For former Indian citizens, but it is not dual citizenship.

question: How does the parliamentary system ensure a “responsible government”? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (16/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: By allowing the President to dismiss the Prime Minister at any time
By giving the judiciary the power to review executive decisions
By permitting the military to oversee governance
By making the council of ministers collectively accountable to the Parliament
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is By making the council of ministers collectively accountable to the Parliament

Explanation:
In a parliamentary system, the key mechanism ensuring a responsible government is the collective accountability of the council of ministers to the Parliament. This means the executive (council of ministers) is answerable to the legislature (Parliament), and if it loses a vote of confidence, it must resign. Thus, the government is indirectly accountable to the people, as Parliament is elected by them. This prevents arbitrary rule and ensures democratic control. The President's powers are limited, the judiciary is independent, and the military has no role in governance. Collective accountability is a core feature of the Westminster model, making the government responsive to public opinion through its representatives.

Explanation:
संसदीय प्रणाली में सरकार की उत्तरदायित्व सुनिश्चित करने का मुख्य तंत्र मंत्रिपरिषद की संसद के प्रति सामूहिक जवाबदेही है। इसका अर्थ है कि कार्यपालिका (मंत्रिपरिषद) विधायिका (संसद) के प्रति उत्तरदायी होती है और यदि वह विश्वास मत खो देती है, तो उसे इस्तीफा देना होता है। इस प्रकार, सरकार जनता के प्रति अप्रत्यक्ष रूप से जवाबदेह बनती है, क्योंकि संसद जनता द्वारा चुनी जाती है। यह सुनिश्चित करता है कि सरकार मनमानी न करे और लोकतांत्रिक नियंत्रण में रहे। राष्ट्रपति की शक्तियां सीमित होती हैं, न्यायपालिका अलग होती है, और सेना का शासन में कोई हस्तक्षेप नहीं होता।

question: Which Constitutional Amendment explicitly inserted the term 'Cabinet' into the Indian Constitution in the context of Article 352? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (16/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976
43rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1977
44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978
45th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1980
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978

Explanation:
The term 'Cabinet' was explicitly inserted into Article 352 of the Indian Constitution by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978. This amendment brought significant changes to the emergency provisions. Prior to this, Article 352 only referred to the 'President' and 'Council of Ministers'. The 44th amendment ensured that a proclamation of emergency could only be issued if the Cabinet (Prime Minister and Cabinet Ministers) gives a written recommendation to the President. This made the procedure for imposing an emergency more stringent. The amendment was introduced to prevent the misuse of emergency powers, ensuring that it could only be declared on the advice of the government. It also replaced the term 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' as a ground for emergency.

☛ What was the purpose of the 44th Amendment regarding emergencies? → To prevent misuse of emergency powers

☛ When was the 44th Amendment enacted? → 1978
☛ Who constitutes the Cabinet? → Prime Minister and Cabinet Ministers

question: Besides resolving disputes, what power do the Nyaya Panchayats have in India? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (17/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Managing village agriculture
Imposing fines on offenders
Issuing binding contracts
Levying taxes for village development
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Imposing fines on offenders

Explanation:
In India, the Nyaya Panchayat is a quasi-judicial body established at the village level. Besides settling disputes, it has the power to impose fines on offenders in minor criminal cases such as assault, theft, and public nuisance. The maximum fine that can be imposed is usually Rs. 100, though it may vary by state. Nyaya Panchayats cannot award imprisonment. They adjudicate civil and criminal matters of a petty nature. Other functions like managing village agriculture, issuing binding contracts, or levying taxes are not within their jurisdiction; these are handled by the Gram Panchayat or other local bodies. Thus, the Nyaya Panchayat primarily focuses on minor judicial functions and imposes fines as a form of punishment. This decentralized system helps in quick justice delivery at the grassroots level.

☛ Can Nyaya Panchayat award imprisonment? → No

question: In March 2025, what important decision did the Supreme Court of India make regarding disability rights? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (19/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: It allowed only private companies to hire persons with disabilities.
It said disability rights are a part of fundamental rights.
It removed reservations for persons with disabilities.
It banned all exams for persons with disabilities.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It said disability rights are a part of fundamental rights.

Explanation:
In March 2025, the Supreme Court of India delivered a landmark judgment declaring that disability rights are an integral part of fundamental rights under the Constitution. The Court ruled that discrimination against persons with disabilities violates Articles 14, 19, and 21. This decision was based on the interpretation of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. The Court emphasized that the state has a duty to ensure equal opportunities for persons with disabilities in both public and private sectors. The judgment strengthened access to education, employment, and public services for disabled individuals. It also affirmed that affirmative action and reservations are essential to fulfill fundamental rights.

question: Which of the following Acts allowed the Crown to take over governance from the East India Company? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (21/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Charter Act, 1813
Ilbert Bill, 1883
Government of India Act, 1858
Indian Councils Act, 1861
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Government of India Act, 1858

Explanation:
The Government of India Act, 1858, also known as the 'Act for the Good Government of India', ended the rule of the East India Company and transferred the governance of India directly to the British Crown. It abolished the Board of Control and the Court of Directors and created the position of Secretary of State for India. The Governor-General received the additional title of Viceroy. The Charter Act of 1813 restricted the Company's trade monopoly, while the Ilbert Bill and Indian Councils Act were later reforms. Thus, this Act marked a significant shift in the administration of India.

question: Which two policy areas are explicitly managed by the Union Cabinet in India as part of its coordinating functions? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Agriculture and Labour
Tourism and Sports
Foreign Relations and Defence
Education and Health
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Foreign Relations and Defence

Explanation:
In India, the Union Cabinet is primarily responsible for coordinating government policies. It directly manages critical areas like Foreign Relations and Defence due to their significance for national security and international affairs. Other options such as Agriculture, Labour, Tourism, Sports, Education, and Health are subjects in the Concurrent List or State List, meaning they are shared with state governments. In contrast, Foreign Relations and Defence are exclusively under the central government's jurisdiction as per the Union List of the Constitution. The Cabinet's coordinating role ensures that various ministries work cohesively, and these two areas require unified decision-making at the highest level to maintain sovereignty and diplomatic integrity.

question: In which landmark case did the Supreme Court of India rule that the Council of Ministers DOES NOT cease to hold office even after the dissolution of the Lok Sabha? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala, 1973
UNR Rao vs. Indira Gandhi, 1971
Golaknath vs. State of Punjab, 1967
SR Bommai vs. Union of India, 1994
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is UNR Rao vs. Indira Gandhi, 1971

Explanation:
In this landmark case, the Supreme Court ruled that the Council of Ministers does not cease to hold office even after the dissolution of the Lok Sabha. The decision pertained to the powers of the President under Article 74. The Court held that the Council of Ministers continues in office until a new government is formed. This ruling was essential to avoid a constitutional crisis. It ensured the continuity of government in a parliamentary democracy. This precedent is crucial for maintaining stability in the exercise of executive powers at the centre. The case clarified that the Council of Ministers acts as an advisory body to the President even during the interim period.

question:
For which of the given bills can the President of India summon a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament?
1. Ordinary Bill
2. Money Bill
3. Constitutional Amendment Bill (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
1 only
2 and 3 only
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1 only

Explanation:
According to Article 108 of the Indian Constitution, the President can summon a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament only for an Ordinary Bill. This happens when one House rejects a bill passed by the other, disagrees on amendments, or does not pass it for more than six months. A joint sitting cannot be called for a Money Bill because the Rajya Sabha can only recommend changes, and the Lok Sabha's decision is final. For a Constitutional Amendment Bill, a joint sitting is also not allowed, as it must be passed separately by each House with a special majority.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which article provides for a joint sitting? → Article 108
☛ For which bills is a joint sitting not allowed? → Money Bill and Constitutional Amendment Bill
☛ Who presides over a joint sitting? → Speaker of Lok Sabha
☛ How many joint sittings have been held so far? → Three (1961, 1978, 2002)
☛ What is required for a Constitutional Amendment Bill? → Special majority in each House

Explanation:
